items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: And Higgenbotham... He was a heck of a trombone player.

ctx.x: Did you get to play with Zutty?

Yes. And Higgenbotham... He was a heck of a trombone player. And Cootie Williams. I told Cootie one time, I said, 'Cootie...' He didn't remember. I know Cootie was with Luis Russell, because he was there at the same time I was. Because he came in there... That was the first band he played with in New York! Luis Russell was a good piano player and he had a job on Lenox Avenue at one of them clubs. I played with him first.

And by the time I got to the Missourians, I was a pretty good musicians by that time, because I'd gone through it with Jelly Roll, and come back to New York... But I'd been ad-libbing all my life, from the days out at school. And when I went to Minot, playing with a little small band, ain't nobody in the band to play solos but you -- and the piano player. Because the guitar didn't do nothin' but strum; he didn't do no pickin'. So I just had that talent to play. And I liked the New Orleans style of playing,…
